claims.text: Adding a 10–30 nm (CrFeTiTa)70W30 interlayer at W–Cu interfaces will reduce interfacial thermal resistance.
Reducing the W–Cu interfacial thermal resistance with this interlayer will enhance the composite's overall thermal conductivity.
A W–Cu composite containing this interlayer will retain mechanical durability.
A W–Cu composite containing this interlayer will retain irradiation resistance.
A conventional W–Cu composite has appreciable interfacial thermal resistance at its W–Cu interfaces.
A HEA film can be fabricated by sputter deposition.
A uniform 10–30 nm (CrFeTiTa)70W30 film can be sputter-deposited onto tungsten particles before W–Cu consolidation.
Annealing around 1100 °C can promote adhesion of the HEA interlayer without causing detrimental interdiffusion if the duration is optimized.
Processing under an inert or reducing atmosphere will prevent oxidation during the proposed treatment.
The deposited HEA will form an adherent interlayer bridging the W and Cu phases.
The HEA interlayer will improve lattice matching between W and Cu.
The HEA interlayer will improve electronic coupling across the W–Cu interface.
Improved lattice matching and electronic coupling will lower electron and phonon scattering at the W–Cu interface.
Lower electron and phonon scattering will improve heat-conduction pathways through the composite.
The refractory HEA has high-temperature mechanical properties that could help preserve interfacial mechanical integrity.
The refractory HEA will provide robust irradiation resistance in the proposed W–Cu interlayer configuration.
The modified composite will have a statistically significant increase in thermal conductivity relative to an otherwise comparable unmodified W–Cu composite.
The modified composite will have comparable or improved mechanical strength relative to the unmodified W–Cu composite.
The modified composite will have comparable or improved irradiation stability relative to the unmodified W–Cu composite.
Layer thickness above 30 nm, poor adhesion, nonuniform deposition, or excessive interdiffusion could compromise performance.
